簡文帝 is the deceased emperor whose second death anniversary falls in 寧康二年, in a court ritual dispute involving Xie An and Huan Chong. He is a reigning-emperor identity with that later court and mourning sequence, whereas Minhuai died as the deposed son of Hui and was restored only as crown prince. The external Xianan conversion in c0826 is not a source identity bridge or fresh date approval.

The named 會稽王昱 participates with Yu Bing, He Chong and Zhuge Hui in accepting Tan’s temple proposal. English Yu Yi in c0376/m0592 conflicts with the Chinese; it does not identify this prince with Minhuai.

虞 is expressly one of Teng’s four sons, avenges Teng by pursuing Li Feng into the water, and is killed with brothers Jiao and Shao by Feng’s remaining party. Minhuai is Hui’s eldest son and is killed by Sun Lü with a pestle while imprisoned. The distinct parentage and death narratives establish separation without relying on 虞/遹 spelling.

簡文帝 ascends after the deposition of Haixi; Huan Wen remains encamped while Sima Tian impeaches him. This enthroned successor in the Haixi/Huan Wen episode cannot be the crown prince whose Minhuai biography reports murder, restoration as crown prince, burial and surviving sons. Teng dispatches 司馬瑜 with Zhou Liang and Shi Xian against Liu Yuanhai’s forces at Lishi/Fencheng; Liu Qin defeats this active commander in four engagements. This is a campaigning officer in Teng’s Han conflict, distinct from the deposed prince murdered in confinement by Sun Lü. Shared Sima Yu romanization is insufficient, and the action/agent sequence supplies positive distinction.

郁 is explicitly Yun’s son and Prince of Qin, killed by Fu Yin along with Yun and Han Prince Di. Hui’s eldest son Minhuai is killed by Sun Lü at Xuchang; Yun is separately present as Prince of Huainan in the Minhuai deposition narrative (s0063). Distinct fathers, titles, agents and death settings establish separation even though both belong to Jin royal unrest.
